flags.message: The upstream supremecourt.gov snapshot (2026-11-03.json) lists LowerCourt as 'United States Bankruptcy Appellate Panel for the 10th Circuit' for LowerCourtCaseNumbers '(26-2404)', even though the application was submitted to The Chief Justice (Circuit Justice for the Fourth Circuit), the Virginia pro se applicant is litigating against an E.D. Va. Chapter 7 bankruptcy trustee (H. Jason Gold), companion application 26A657 (from No. 26-2406) lists the Fourth Circuit, and CourtListener confirms that No. 26-2404 is In re: Paul Schultz in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit (arising from E.D. Va. No. 1:26-cv-02804-LMB-IDD).

The application was fetched (57 pages), but documents.json marks empty_text=true and ocr_derived=false; application.txt contains no usable content. Prediction completed from the submission docket and prior-Term interim rates without assessing the application's arguments. OCR or usable filing text would materially improve the forecast; this is not a missing-snapshot or absent-filing claim.

Staged application.txt is empty_text (no text layer) on a 57-page PDF; forecast made from docket and base rates. Also: lower court listed as BAP for the 10th Circuit, but applicant is in Virginia and the application went to the Chief Justice (4th Cir. Circuit Justice); the 4th Circuit has no BAP, so the lower-court label may be wrong.

Provisioned `record/documents/application.txt` (61 pages) has `empty_text: true` and `ocr_derived: false` (scanned pro se filing with no extractable text layer). The subject matter of the underlying Fourth Circuit proceeding (No. 26-2406, `In re: Paul Schultz`, denying mandamus to compel District Judge Brinkema's recusal in a bankruptcy appeal against Chapter 7 Trustee Kevin McCarthy) was verified via CourtListener (`opinion_id: 11514107`).

The 61-page application was provisioned with empty_text=true and ocr_derived=false; application.txt contains only page separators. The arrival snapshot identifies neither the challenged order nor the legal grounds or harm. The forecast therefore rests principally on the private/unmarked application prior, not a substantive reading of the application. A bounded Fourth Circuit docket search returned no matches. This is an extraction/content limitation, not an absent filing or a failure to locate the case-level record; the prediction is complete.

The snapshot lists a September 15, 2026 supplemental response by petitioner, but documents.json and supplemental-brief.txt stage only respondents' September 14 supplemental brief, despite the manifest's description of combined supplemental filings. Respondents report dismissal without prejudice and planned amendment; petitioner's answer to that development is unavailable. Forecast completed without inventing its contents or assuming the amended pleading's status.

Source dates are not internally reconciled: the snapshot's petition entry says February 6, 2026, docketing is September 21, 2026, and the petition bears April 2026 and claims an April 16 extension deadline. These may reflect different processing acts, but the record does not explain the sequence. Used the supplied pending posture and December 4 conference; did not infer untimeliness or dismissal from the ambiguity.

The appendix table of contents lists underlying pleadings and exhibits beyond App-27, but the provisioned public text ends after App-27 with a notice that additional material is available in the Clerk's Office. Metadata marks the file not truncated. The actual complaint, proposed amendment, and evidentiary exhibits therefore could not be audited directly; this is not assumed to be a pipeline truncation or an absence of those materials.

Private contact information remains in appendix correspondence around App-7 despite documents.json reporting contact_scrubbed=true and contact_residuals=0. No contact value is reproduced here or elsewhere in this cell, and none informed the forecast. Please review the correspondence-address scrub coverage.

Companion petition No. 25-1246 (same petitioner, same Brady/second-or-successive issue, record requested, set for the same 12/4/2026 conference) was not staged under record/related/ because the docket carries no Vide link. I retrieved it from supremecourt.gov, and it moved the forecast.

record/context.json froze band='baseline' (cert_anchor.rate=0.051513) rather than 'federal' under sal-v7 because the docket caption 'National Park Service, et al., Petitioners' lacks 'United States' or a cabinet-officer title matched by the caption classifier, even though Solicitor General D. John Sauer is counsel of record for federal agencies and the President of the United States.

The authoritative context freezes sal-v7 band baseline and cert_anchor.rate 0.051512996760685784, although the petitioners are the National Park Service and other federal parties represented by the Solicitor General. This appears inconsistent with the prompt's federal caption-class arrival guidance and may affect the scoring benchmark. I preserve the supplied conditioning unchanged, acknowledge its 652/12657 strictly-prior baseline pool, and separately use the published federal arrival comparison of 155/212 (73.11%) over Terms 2017-2025. The high forecast rests principally on the provisioned August 31 stay opinion, not on reclassifying the harness's band. Please review the caption classification.

context.json froze band 'baseline' (cert_anchor 0.0515, the private-class floor), but the caption is a federal petitioner (National Park Service et al., President Trump; SG D. John Sauer counsel of record). The caption-class rule should read 'federal' (pooled reached rate about 73%). The forecast anchors on the federal floor; scoring against 0.05 will misstate skill.

In record/snapshots/2026-11-07.json, RelatedCaseNumber[0] has DisplayCaseNumber='26-199, 26-201, 26-332, 26-335' and RelatedType='Vide', but context.json has vide_links=[] and no record/related/ snapshots were provisioned, likely because DisplayCaseNumber contained comma-separated docket numbers in one entry. Companion dockets were inspected via fedcourts query --court scotus --docket-number.

The snapshot lists a separate October 13, 2026 federal respondents' opposition memorandum. The provisioned brief-in-opposition.txt contains the Authority's brief rather than that separate federal memorandum. A web open of its predecision docket link returned no usable content. The forecast uses the available private BIO and does not infer the federal memorandum's recommendation; prediction completed despite this limited gap.

Snapshot carries RelatedCaseNumber Vide links (26-199, 26-201, 26-332, 26-335) but context.json has vide_links: [] and no record/related/ was staged; companion status was read from supremecourt.gov instead.

Harness check: this cell's logged tool calls named a committed predictions/ or evaluations/ path other than this cell's own run directory (another predictor's output, an earlier run, or a glob over them): 1 call(s), e.g. 'predictions/**/prediction.json'. Read from retrieval_log.json, which records that a call named the path, not what it returned; check the transcript before treating it as a read.

The snapshot describes the filing only as a petition for certiorari. The official DOJ petition expressly seeks certiorari before judgment, a material vehicle distinction not visible in the staged docket text. Forecast incorporates that retrieved posture. Expected paper-only document absence is not a provisioning failure; no current-petition outcome was retrieved.

Snapshot's first entry reads 'Petition for a writ of certiorari filed', but the live supremecourt.gov docket reads 'Petition for a writ of certiorari before judgment filed'. The posture matters for the forecast; the snapshot text seems to have been normalized or captured before the Clerk amended it.

Frozen band is 'baseline' (cert_anchor 5.15%), but this petition is filed by the Solicitor General (D. John Sauer, counsel of record) on behalf of individual federal DEA task-force officers. The caption names only the officers, so the caption-class scorer reads it as private. In substance it belongs in the 'federal' class (pooled reached rate ~70%). Forecast departs from the frozen anchor accordingly.

Prediction-time statpack coverage cannot be reconstructed from staged result contents: claude-baseline, codex-baseline and gemini-baseline all report zero finer-resolved observations in their earlier pack, whereas the current committed OT2016–OT2025 pool has 1,337 finer-resolved and zero finer-unread observations. I preserved this apparent pack-vintage distinction, did not infer a candidate audit error from today's counts, and left baseline/skill values to the harness. This did not block evaluation.

gemini-baseline quotes the opening entry as an immediate administrative stay/stay pending appeal submitted to Justice Gorsuch and bases its standard/referral analysis on that description. The staged resolved docket instead says an injunction submitted to the Chief Justice; the application is addressed to Roberts and expressly distinguishes its affirmative All Writs Act injunction from a stay. This materially affects the rationale and forecast grades. The original candidate snapshot is not staged, so the origin of the historical-input versus prose mismatch cannot be established.

All three candidates describe application.txt as empty/non-OCR at prediction time. This evaluation receives 29,507 bytes of readable application text with empty_text=false and ocr_derived=true. The refreshed OCR was used to check the nature of the event, not imputed to candidates as information they had. No candidate is penalized merely for not analyzing the newly readable filing.

Historical baseline assertions cannot be fully reconciled from the staged evidence: claude-baseline reports zero finer-resolved counts/unread prior Terms, codex-baseline reports an older markdown table without finer counts, and gemini-baseline reports a populated finer pool. The current JSON pack has positive finer counts and zero finer_unread in 2016–2025, with several counts differing from gemini-baseline's table. Original statpack bytes/result bodies are not staged; pack evolution cannot be distinguished from misreading. No alternate baseline is supplied and the stamp remains authoritative.
